source_basis: The object of our model is to provide an emergency evacuation for the Louvre. In the meantime, this model can also identify potential bottlenecks. However, complex building structures and the interaction among people makes the problem much harder.
interpretation: The job is named, a second job is added, and the difficulty is conceded in the third sentence.
applicability: Open a summary with the job, a second job, and the difficulty that stands in the way.
counterevidence: The difficulty is asserted, not measured.

source_basis: The effect will be ultimately reflected in the flow speed of the crowd. In this way, while calculating the flow speed of the crowd, we adopt N&M model and Stable Evacuation Speed model to deal with different situation.
interpretation: Every individual factor is collapsed into one quantity, and the two tools are named for it.
applicability: Say where an effect lands before naming the tools used to compute it.
counterevidence: The sentence says the effect lands in speed but does not show the landing.

source_basis: Then simplify the problem from muti-to-muti plan to single-to-single plan through adding two virtual nodes. This step makes the following solution much easier.
interpretation: A reduction is sold by the work it saves.
applicability: Justify a simplification by naming what it removes and what that saves.
counterevidence: The saving is claimed before the reduction is shown.

source_basis: In this way, the algorithm can carry out route planning from the perspective of system, and fully consider the micro factors.
interpretation: Both scales are claimed in one sentence.
applicability: Claim a whole-building view and the small factors together only when both are modeled.
counterevidence: The small factors enter only through the speed, so the claim is broader than the model.

source_basis: The model obtains the result within 0.457s with a scale of 770 people. Besides, to a certain extent, the result matches practical case.
interpretation: A runtime and a size are given, and the match to practice is hedged.
applicability: Report compute time and scale, and keep the hedge on any match to practice.
counterevidence: No practical case is cited, so the match has nothing behind it.

source_basis: It cost 36.15s to get the result with a scale of 6700 people and accuracy of 0.1s. The total evacuation cost 288.7s.
interpretation: Compute time, scale, step and total evacuation time are stacked in two sentences.
applicability: Keep compute time separate from the evacuation time it produces.
counterevidence: Section 7.2 later says the hall holds about 7000, not 6700.

source_basis: Museums, libraries, and exhibition halls around the world are paying more attention to the safe evacuation of venues, and are looking for suitable emergency evacuation methods. Therefore, it is vital to establish a widely used and adaptable emergency evacuation model.
interpretation: A trend is made to earn the model.
applicability: Derive the need for a model from a stated trend.
counterevidence: The trend is not sourced.

source_basis: Among them, Wakim proposed a Markov pedestrian model; Helbing proposed a social force model. The above models are very suitable for the study of individual movement. However, for a large, multi-story venue, an evacuation model with a general view from the whole to the local is needed.
interpretation: Two models are credited, granted their strength, then outgrown.
applicability: Praise the cited work before saying what it cannot do.
counterevidence: The cited models are not shown to fail on this building.

source_basis: Due to the diversity of visitors and the complex structure of the building, it poses a great challenge to safe evacuation. We need to develop an emergency evacuation model to provide museum staff with options.
interpretation: Two causes make one challenge, and the challenge makes the deliverable.
applicability: Name the causes before the challenge and the challenge before the deliverable.
counterevidence: The doubled phrase options for evacuation options is a slip, not a device.

source_basis: The established model needs to accomplish the following objectives. At the same time, the model should consider several implicit objectives.
interpretation: What the prompt asked is separated from what the team inferred.
applicability: Mark implied objectives as implied.
counterevidence: The implied list is the team's reading, not the prompt's.

source_basis: In our research program, the first step is the microscopic part. The second step is to establish a spatial node graph. The third step is the macro part. The final step is to promote the model.
interpretation: The method is given as four steps ordered by scale.
applicability: Lay a method out as numbered steps before the detail.
counterevidence: The fourth step is only sketched.

source_basis: 1. The guiding signs and notifications of the venues are clear enough. 2. The vast majority of people are rational enough to follow the signs. 4. The crowd will not evacuate in opposite directions.
interpretation: Five assumptions are numbered and none is given a reason.
applicability: A bare assumption list promises no justification and should not be read as one.
counterevidence: Assumption 4 forbids counter-flow while the corridor matrix is symmetric.

source_basis: Note: Symbols not mentioned in the table will be explained if they appear below.
interpretation: The table is kept short by promising the rest later.
applicability: Defer a symbol only if it is defined where it first appears.
counterevidence: The table as extracted has a blank unit and a unit printed as a backslash.

source_basis: According to the related research of Predtechenski and Milinskii, the average evacuation speed is a function of the flow density. Unfortunately, this is a complex nonlinear relationship, that is not suitable for a wide range of applications.
interpretation: A source is credited and then declined for a stated reason.
applicability: Reject a cited relation only with the reason for the rejection.
counterevidence: The nonlinear curve is never shown, so the rejection rests on the citation.

source_basis: After that, Nelson and Mowrer et al. simplified the relationship between velocity and flow density to a linear relationship, and selected different linear coefficients for different evacuation channels.
interpretation: The simplification is credited to its authors rather than claimed.
applicability: Credit a simplification to its source before using it.
counterevidence: The coefficient table is cited as reference [5], which the reference list does not match cleanly.

source_basis: In summary, N&M Model considers the relationship between evacuation speed and flow density, but it is not suitable for the situation where the flow density is relatively large. So we try to find a better model to replace it.
interpretation: A model is closed by the case it fails, which opens the search for the next one.
applicability: End a model section on the gap the next section fills.
counterevidence: The replacement that follows is never coded.

source_basis: The distance from the previous person is |xj - xj-1|, which is recorded as A. The relative velocity is recorded as B. Then the forward damping force caused by crowding is proportional to B/A.
interpretation: Two quantities are lettered in speech before the proportion that uses them.
applicability: Name and letter a quantity before it enters a formula.
counterevidence: The letters A and B are reused later for different quantities.

source_basis: Note that Side-Crowding is generally suitable when the crowd density is particularly large, and when the population density is small, it has little effect.
interpretation: A term is bounded in the same sentence that introduces it.
applicability: State where a term applies and where it does not, together.
counterevidence: No density is given for the boundary between the two cases.

source_basis: According to Newton's second law, we have obtained the following escape velocity dynamics equation.
interpretation: The law is named and the equation follows.
applicability: Name the law a displayed equation comes from.
counterevidence: The printed equation carries a minus on the left, which the second law does not.

source_basis: When the density is small, the velocity of the human flow is not affected by it, and the critical density does not affect the velocity.
interpretation: The regime where density drops out is said in words before the formula.
applicability: State a regime in speech next to the formula that encodes it.
counterevidence: The critical densities are given later, so the regime has no numbers here.

source_basis: It is analyzed that the above model is a generalized model. When the flow density is large, neither of alpha, beta, gamma is zero. When smaller, mainly Front-Crowding; when small enough, only personnel characteristics, and v is a certain value.
interpretation: One formula is read as three regimes.
applicability: Unpack a single formula into the regimes it covers.
counterevidence: The weights are never given values, so the regimes cannot be located.

source_basis: The only downside is that due to the uncertainty and ambiguity of the characteristics of the personnel, the effect of this part on the whole cannot be well described.
interpretation: A model is closed by naming exactly one weakness.
applicability: Close a model with its single real weakness, not a list.
counterevidence: Other weaknesses exist, so the word only overclaims.

source_basis: To simplify the calculation, we added two hypothetical nodes 1 and 9.
interpretation: An addition is justified by the arithmetic it saves.
applicability: Introduce a device by the work it removes.
counterevidence: The nodes are justified only by convenience, not by a conservation argument.

source_basis: This creates a new single goal to single goal issue. This result corresponds to the relationship between the total number of people remaining in all rooms and the flow of people leaving all exits. The simplification of the goal brings great convenience to the optimization of the algorithm.
interpretation: The reduced problem is restated as the relation it now stands for.
applicability: After a reduction, say what the new variables correspond to.
counterevidence: The prose counts six rooms numbered 2 to 7 while the figure shows nodes 2 to 8.

source_basis: From the matrix point of view, this shows that the human traffic matrix is a symmetrical matrix, and the diagonal line is all zero because it has no practical meaning.
interpretation: A physical statement is translated into a matrix property, with the reason.
applicability: Give the matrix reading and the reason for it in one sentence.
counterevidence: Symmetry encodes flow in both directions, which assumption 4 rules out.

source_basis: In order to get the maximum of escape speed, we need to make full use of the channel resources at any time to maximize the escape rate. In the established model, the problem is equivalent to obtaining the maximum flow from the source to the sink at any time.
interpretation: The goal is renamed as a standard problem.
applicability: State an equivalence explicitly and only when it holds.
counterevidence: The equivalence holds only if each time step can be treated as steady.

source_basis: The resulting stream at this point is the maximum flow, which can be proved by the maximum flow minimum cut theorem. And we will not prove this here.
interpretation: A theorem is leaned on and the proof is openly declined.
applicability: Name the theorem and say the proof is not given, rather than skipping silently.
counterevidence: The citation for the theorem is a Chinese applied-mathematics note, not the original.

source_basis: Therefore, we properly use the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm in the solution of the problem and propose a dynamic system planning algorithm based on the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm.
interpretation: The standard method is kept and the change is given its own name.
applicability: Say what was kept and what was changed before naming a new method.
counterevidence: The change is the outer time loop; the inner method is unaltered.

source_basis: It can be seen intuitively that the first step of the evacuation plan is to empty the exit rooms. Then the personnel at the second-level nodes move to the adjacent first-level nodes. Then the flow is even reduced to 0.
interpretation: A figure is read back as an ordered plan.
applicability: Turn a flow figure into a sequence of actions.
counterevidence: The reading is the team's; the figure shows flows, not instructions.

source_basis: We divide them into three categories: bottlenecks due to channel supply and demand imbalances, bottlenecks due to uneven distribution of exports, and single room export bottlenecks.
interpretation: The count and the names come before the cases.
applicability: Announce a classification and then treat every class named.
counterevidence: The three classes overlap: a narrow door is also a supply limit.

source_basis: In order to solve the problem, we choose to expand the width of the restricted channel while keep the density unchanged. The total evacuation time is about 43.2s.
interpretation: A fix is named and the time after it is reported.
applicability: Report the changed time next to the fix that produced it.
counterevidence: The accuracy is said to depend on the time step, which is not varied.

source_basis: Let's take a fire accident in a room as an example to show that our model is adaptable.
interpretation: One case is offered as the proof of adaptability.
applicability: Mark a single example as an example, not as coverage.
counterevidence: The emergency branch that performs this case is commented out in the code.

source_basis: We give two options for this. Combined with domestic and foreign rescue cases, our program meets the actual requirements.
interpretation: Two options are given and then said to match practice.
applicability: A match to practice needs a cited case.
counterevidence: No rescue case is cited.

source_basis: From the simulation, we can summarize the following conclusions: at the beginning keep the exit area open, in the middle open other exits, in the later stage allow rescuers to enter.
interpretation: One run is turned into three timed actions.
applicability: Stage the conclusions so each one points at a part of the run.
counterevidence: The three stages are read off the figures, not computed as thresholds.

source_basis: In order to give museum personnel a complete model exploration method, we give the following suggestions.
interpretation: Advice is framed as a method the staff can follow.
applicability: Address recommendations to the user and tie each one to a result.
counterevidence: Several steps repeat the model's own inputs as if they were findings.

source_basis: It can be seen that the model can guarantee the accuracy of the simulation within a certain error range. To a certain extent, the model can eliminate the impact of errors through iterative updating.
interpretation: A sensitivity figure is read as a guarantee, and the guarantee is hedged.
applicability: Keep the hedge when a figure only covers one error size.
counterevidence: Only a five percent density error is tried.

source_basis: The model has great generalization because it does not consider any special circumstances but the general situation.
interpretation: A strength is claimed together with its reason.
applicability: Give the reason in the same sentence as the claim.
counterevidence: Generalization is argued from the absence of special cases, which is weak.

source_basis: In order to fully exert its dynamic capabilities, it may be necessary to monitor the flow density of the channel and the exit. Thus there are certain limitations.
interpretation: A requirement is restated as the limitation.
applicability: Name the requirement that bounds the model.
counterevidence: The limitation is real but loosely stated.

source_basis: When there is a special case for each value in the graph, the algorithm will loop indefinitely. However, considering that we apply the algorithm to the human flow problem, the probability of occurrence in a special case is almost zero.
interpretation: A known failure is stated and then judged unlikely for this use.
applicability: Keep almost zero as a judgment, not a proof.
counterevidence: The paper cites the non-termination result and does not bound it.

source_basis: The reference list runs from pedestrian models and the SFPE handbook to a museum floor plan.
interpretation: The list mixes method papers, a handbook and a plan.
applicability: Treat the list as this paper's own bibliography.
counterevidence: One speed-coefficient citation points at an entry that does not match the table.

source_basis: Equation (1) sets v = k - 0.266 k D for density between 0.54 and 3.8 persons per square metre, with k = 1 on stairs and k = 1.4 in corridors.
interpretation: One line, two coefficients, covers the ordinary channels.
applicability: Record a borrowed speed law with its stated window and the coefficients chosen.
counterevidence: The code uses k = 1.08 for stairs.

source_basis: Equations (2) to (8) build a speed from front crowding, side crowding and a trait term, and equation (8) is the speed the staircase matrix uses.
interpretation: The crowded-channel speed is derived rather than borrowed.
applicability: Keep the derived speed next to the channel that consumes it.
counterevidence: The derivation has a sign error, an undefined substitution and four underived coefficients.

source_basis: Equation (14) sets the overall matrix G equal to the sum of the corridor, staircase, initial and export matrices.
interpretation: Four matrices with different meanings are added into the one the algorithm reads.
applicability: Record the sum and what each part contributes.
counterevidence: The parts have different units, so the sum mixes persons and persons per second.

source_basis: Each iteration is one time period, derives the flow matrix and the margin matrix, corrects the room counts, and resets each channel capacity from its density, stopping below 0.5 people at the source.
interpretation: The outer loop is the part the paper adds to Ford-Fulkerson.
applicability: Describe a dynamic wrapper by what it updates each step and when it stops.
counterevidence: The emergency branch of the same loop is commented out in the code.

source_basis: The test building draws node populations as random numbers between 100 and 200 and sets exit capacities at 40, 35 and 30 persons per second.
interpretation: The verification case is synthetic.
applicability: Mark a test case as synthetic when no measured counts are used.
counterevidence: Random counts cannot confirm a real building.

source_basis: Node 6 has two inlets of 15 and 12.1 against an outlet of 30, so the flow is limited by supply, and widening that channel removes the dip.
interpretation: A bottleneck is pinned to a number comparison.
applicability: Show a bottleneck as inlet sum against outlet capacity.
counterevidence: The inlet values are read off a figure and not tabulated.

source_basis: Figure 13 shows the exit flow starting near 140 persons per second, stepping down to about 118, holding until roughly 250 seconds and collapsing to near zero by about 290 seconds.
interpretation: The five-minute claim matches the curve.
applicability: Check a stated total time against the curve that shows it.
counterevidence: The curve is read from a proxy, so the intermediate levels are approximate.

source_basis: The Louvre is split into five floors, each reduced to a plane node map, with stairs as the links between floors, and the head count placed by room size.
interpretation: A real plan is reduced to a graph by hand.
applicability: Record the reduction and the rule used to place people.
counterevidence: The room-size weights are not given.

source_basis: Figure 15 shows the original and the plus or minus five percent density curves nearly overlapping and separating only at the final drop, for both the test building and the Louvre.
interpretation: One error size leaves the result nearly unchanged.
applicability: Report a sensitivity test by the range tried and where the curves split.
counterevidence: A single error size is not a sensitivity study.

source_basis: The crowd will not evacuate in opposite directions, while equation (9) sets the corridor flow equal in both directions.
interpretation: The assumption and the matrix disagree.
applicability: Record a conflict between an assumption and an equation rather than smoothing it.
counterevidence: The symmetry may mean capacity rather than simultaneous flow.

source_basis: Equation (2) is printed as minus m_j times the acceleration equal to the damping force plus the friction, so a positive damping force accelerates the person the prose says is slowed.
interpretation: The printed sign contradicts the stated mechanism.
applicability: Keep a sign conflict as a warning on the equation, not as the paper's result.
counterevidence: An overall sign convention could rescue it, but none is stated.

source_basis: The appendix code computes corridor speed as 1 - 0.266 times 1.40 times density and stair speed as 1 - 0.266 times 1.08 times density, and the whole emergency-handling block is commented out.
interpretation: The stable evacuation model is never executed, and the stair coefficient differs from the prose.
applicability: Compare the code with the prose and record the gap.
counterevidence: The code may be a simplified demonstration rather than the reported run.

source_basis: The paper sets rho = rho_1 times rho_2 = D, multiplying two persons-per-metre densities into persons squared per square metre and equating the product to a persons-per-square-metre congestion.
interpretation: The two densities are combined in a way that breaks the units.
applicability: Record a unit break where a derived quantity is set equal to one with different units.
counterevidence: The product may be intended as a product of dimensionless ratios.

source_basis: Figure 3 puts a source node and a sink node around the rooms, and the prose says six rooms numbered 2 to 7 while the figure shows nodes 2 to 8.
interpretation: The figure and the prose count the rooms differently.
applicability: Check a figure's labels against the sentence that introduces it.
counterevidence: Node 8 may be an exit rather than a room, which the prose does not say.

source_basis: Figure 4 draws the overall matrix as a block with the initial strip on top, the export strip on the right and the channel core in the middle.
interpretation: The block picture is what makes the four-matrix sum readable.
applicability: Use a block diagram when a matrix is assembled from parts.
counterevidence: The figure was read from a proxy and the labels are small.

source_basis: Figure 14 colours the margin red where a channel is fully loaded and blue where it has spare capacity, and the prose says the route can be replanned from the blue lines near the red ones.
interpretation: The margin plot is the bottleneck device for the real building.
applicability: Read a margin plot as the place where replanning is decided.
counterevidence: The panel was not inspected on the raster.

source_basis: Flow Margin is defined as maximum flow minus actual flow, and the paper says that to minimise evacuation time the margin must be minimised.
interpretation: A new quantity is defined and tied to the objective.
applicability: Define a diagnostic quantity by the decision it changes.
counterevidence: Minimising every margin is not the same as minimising the time.

source_basis: The paper says the storage will occupy a large amount of space as precision rises, yet for a general building it stays within acceptable limits.
interpretation: A cost is named and then bounded by judgment.
applicability: State a cost and the bound claimed for it.
counterevidence: No storage figure is given.
